source_metadata.title: Effects of Intensive Glucose Lowering in Type 2 Diabetes
source_metadata.group_author: The Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes Study Group

atoms.canonical_statement: ACCORD tested whether an intensive strategy targeting near-normal glycated hemoglobin would reduce major cardiovascular events compared with a strategy targeting glycated hemoglobin 7.0-7.9% in high-risk adults with type 2 diabetes.

population.label: ACCORD glycemia-trial participants with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors

atoms.canonical_statement: The glycemia trial was a randomized multicenter study conducted at 77 clinical centers in the United States and Canada within a double two-by-two factorial ACCORD design that also tested blood-pressure or lipid interventions.

population.label: ACCORD glycemia-trial participants with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible participants had type 2 diabetes with glycated hemoglobin at least 7.5% and either established cardiovascular disease at age 40-79 years or, at age 55-79 years, evidence of atherosclerosis, albuminuria, left ventricular hypertrophy, or at least two additional cardiovascular risk factors; key exclusions included recent serious hypoglycemia, inability to follow intensive monitoring/injection procedures, BMI >45, creatinine >1.5 mg/dL, or serious illness.

population.label: Adults screened for ACCORD glycemia randomization
inclusion_criteria: Age 40-79 with cardiovascular disease OR age 55-79 with specified high-risk features
exclusion_criteria: Unwillingness to self-monitor glucose or inject insulin

atoms.canonical_statement: A total of 10,251 participants were randomized; mean age was 62.2 years, median baseline glycated hemoglobin was 8.1%, 38% were women, and 35% had a previous cardiovascular event.

population.label: ACCORD glycemia-trial participants with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors

atoms.canonical_statement: The intensive glycemia strategy targeted glycated hemoglobin below 6.0%, used any available glucose-lowering drugs in individualized combinations, and used frequent treatment contacts to intensify therapy.

concept.text: Comprehensive intensive glucose-lowering strategy targeting glycated hemoglobin <6.0%

exposures.details: Individualized multidrug strategy with frequent visits and therapy adjustment.

atoms.canonical_statement: The standard glycemia strategy targeted glycated hemoglobin 7.0-7.9% with individualized glucose-lowering therapy and less frequent glycemic-management visits.

concept.text: Standard glucose-lowering strategy targeting glycated hemoglobin 7.0-7.9%

exposures.details: Individualized standard glycemic strategy.

atoms.canonical_statement: The prespecified primary outcome was the first occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes.

concept.text: First occurrence of nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke, or death from cardiovascular causes

atoms.canonical_statement: Key cardiovascular outcomes and deaths were centrally adjudicated by reviewers unaware of glycemia-treatment assignment, and glycated hemoglobin was measured in a central laboratory blinded to treatment assignment.

population.label: ACCORD glycemia-trial participants with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors

atoms.canonical_statement: Primary and secondary time-to-event analyses followed the intention-to-treat principle and used Cox proportional-hazards models to estimate hazard ratios with 95% confidence intervals; the trial was planned for 89% power to detect a 15% reduction in the primary outcome.

population.label: ACCORD glycemia-trial participants with type 2 diabetes and established cardiovascular disease or additional cardiovascular risk factors

atoms.canonical_statement: An independent data and safety monitoring committee reviewed accumulating safety and efficacy data approximately every six months and recommended stopping the intensive glycemia regimen after observing excess mortality; participants were subsequently transitioned to standard glycemic therapy.

atoms.canonical_statement: The trial was not designed to identify which component of the intensive glycemia strategy caused the excess mortality or to determine the optimal rate of glycated hemoglobin reduction; postrandomization treatment differences therefore cannot establish mechanism.

The findings do not directly address people with baseline glycated hemoglobin below 7.5%, diabetes prevention, lower-risk patients without established cardiovascular disease or additional risk factors, or the subgroup hypotheses suggested by exploratory interaction analyses.

The authors concluded that, compared with standard therapy, an intensive strategy targeting normal glycated hemoglobin for a mean 3.5 years increased mortality and did not significantly reduce major cardiovascular events in this high-risk type 2 diabetes population.
